jobs.brief: Jeonju to Nonsan in western inland South Korea. Left edge low weathered market-neighborhood roofs at a gentle basin edge; broad open agricultural lowlands throughout the middle, drainage channels, muted harvested fields and scattered low farm sheds; right edge continues the SAME farmland with a few village roofs. Far rounded hills remain very low and distant throughout, not a mountain wall. No coast, seaport, city skyline, peaks or snow. This is a compressed inference about lowland terrain, not an exact surveyed road.

jobs.brief: Wonju to Daegwallyeong, WEST TO EAST reading left to right. One continuous Korean forested upland valley, layered gently rounded ridges across the whole panorama. Left small foothill settlement at the very edge, sparse roof fragments, restrained vegetation. Across middle the forested slopes slowly draw closer and cultivated clearings become smaller; right an open highland saddle with conifer edges and a tiny weathered roadside shed. Keep the SAME ridgeline family, weather and scale. No abrupt snow, no alpine rock needles, no sea, no giant cliff, no famous landmark.

jobs.brief: Daegwallyeong toward Gangneung, one continuous EASTERN SLOPE valley vista. Rounded densely forested ridge on the left gradually lowers and opens across the whole panorama into distant coastal lowland on the right, where only a subtle slim pale-blue sea band is glimpsed beyond fields and a few low roofs. The sea must occupy LESS than the final quarter of the strip and remain distant. Continuous overlapping forested foothills connect all parts, not one mountain scene pasted beside one beach scene. No sheer alpine cliff dropping into sea, no snow, no harbor cranes, no skyscrapers. Korean pine vegetation, neutral season, subdued cool blue-gray.
